submission.justification: Module-D2 at 30% coverage gave the highest simulated light collection: 52.3 PE/MeV, against 37.6 for D3 at 30%. The 2025 study at 20% coverage had the same ranking (38, 27 and 18 PE/MeV for D2, D3 and D1). Light collection rises with coverage, and the meeting notes say enough feedthroughs exist for 30%. Caveat: D2 uses a thin bonded dichroic filter, and no document reports a cryogenic or long-term robustness test for it. I could not confirm robustness for any design, so it should be verified (for example by thermal-cycling the bond) before the Q3 design freeze. I did not simulate D1 at 30%.

requirements.evidence: D2 at 30% gave 52.3 PE/MeV in simulation, against 37.6 for D3 at 30%. In the 2025 study at 20%, D1 was the lowest at 18 PE/MeV. I did not simulate D1 at 30%.

requirements.requirement: Module is one of the three listed designs
Modules robust, since they are inaccessible after the cryostat is filled
requirements.evidence: The documents contain no robustness or cryogenic test data. D2's thin bonded dichroic filter is a possible delamination risk. The cold electronics are validated for all designs, and argon purity is expected to be good.
30% is the upper limit. Feedthroughs are sufficient for up to 30%.

requirements.requirement: Submit one recommended design and coverage
